assessments.reasoning: After confirming property presence in a with environment, HasBinding reads @@unscopables. If it obtains an object, it retrieves the flag under the same name and converts it to Boolean. A true result makes this record report false. Section 9.1.2.1 establishes the scope limit by continuing identifier lookup in the outer environment after that result.

challenge.method: Trace a truthy non-Boolean flag with an outer binding, then vary the with marker, the unscopables value and completion of the flag read.
challenge.results: The truthy flag blocks this record and permits lookup to reach the outer binding. For a present property, a false with marker bypasses the filter, and a non-object unscopables value leaves the binding visible. A throwing flag read propagates.

limitations: This concerns one environment record's binding check. Other records in the chain can still bind the name.
The outcome assumes all reached accesses complete normally. The flag is tested using the edition's ToBoolean operation, which also specifies an Annex B variant in §B.3.6.1.
